title: Parrot: Free, open-source AI meeting recorder for Mac
excerpt: A meeting recorder for your Mac with a live AI assistant. Answers from your own documents, mid-call. Free and open source.
content_html:
New in 0.25.2fewer echoes in your transcript

AI meeting recorder and live assistant for MacHelp during the call.
Not after it.

Parrot is a meeting recorder for your Mac with a live AI assistant built in. It notices when a call starts, suggests answers from your own documents while you're still talking, and remembers every call so you can ask about it later. The audio stays on your Mac. Free and open source.

Type a line or two before you hit record, and the Assistant knows who you're talking to. Your documents are already in play.

  • No bot joins your meeting

    Parrot records what your Mac already plays and hears. Nothing shows up in the participant list.

  • Audio stays on your Mac

    Transcription, speaker detection and your documents run on your own machine. Cloud transcription happens only if you switch it on.

  • Works with anything that makes sound

    Google Meet, Zoom, Teams, a phone on speaker. If your Mac can hear it, Parrot can. When a call app starts, it asks whether to record.

  • Open source, GPL-3.0
  • No account
  • No telemetry
  • Auto-detects your language
  • Signed and notarized
  • macOS 14+, Apple Silicon

Knowledge base

Brief it like a new teammate.

Drop in your pricing sheet, your FAQ, your playbook. Parrot reads them on your Mac and answers from them on the call.

Drop in a PDF, a text file, or markdown.

Your documents stay here

PDF, text or markdown, in most languages. They're chunked and embedded on this Mac with Apple's own language models. Nothing is uploaded, ever. An English question can even find the answer in a Turkish or Spanish document.

It says where an answer came from

Every card names its source: your document, or the words general knowledge. You decide whether it may answer beyond your files at all.

Coaching instructions and a pre-call brief

Standing guidance for every call, like keep answers short and always offer three price options. And one line before you hit record, so the Assistant knows who you're talking to from the first second. Meeting the same people again? It starts with what's still open from last time.

Profiles

One app, every kind of call.

Tell Parrot what kind of call it is. The profile decides what the Assistant watches for while you talk, and how the report is written after. Use one of seven, or make your own.

Sales discovery watches for objections and buying signals, and asks what you forgot to.

Profile

Live, it changes what the Assistant watches for

Each profile has its own card types and gauges. Sales looks for objections and buying signals. An interview looks for red flags and strong answers.

After, it changes how the report is written

The report is written about the prospect, the candidate or the customer, and follows the profile's own rules.

Make your own

Start from one of seven built-ins or from scratch. Name it, say who the other side is, write your rules, pick its documents, add card types and gauges.

Picked by your calendar

Connect your calendar and an event called Interview: Jane picks your Interview profile. Set a profile to on-device only, and nothing about those calls leaves your Mac.

The brain

You pick the brain.

Run the AI on your Mac with Ollama, or bring a key for Claude, OpenAI, Gemini and more. Each choice says exactly what it sends.

AssistantClaudeOllamaOpenAIGeminiGroqOpenRouterLM Studio

TranscriptionWhisper on your MacParakeet on your MacGroqDeepgram

Doc answers in a secondTypeSafe AINew

Claude writes the sharpest cards. Add a TypeSafe key and the right line from your documents lands within a second.

Assistant

Transcription

Pause

One button on the call screen. While paused nothing is sent and nothing is spent.

Pace

Relaxed fits free tiers. Fast is for calls where every second counts. You also choose how much of the conversation each request carries.

Live nudges

A short tip over the call app when it drifts: "They've gone quiet since you said 'the price goes up in January'." It reads timing and words, never the tone of anyone's voice. Turn it off in Settings under Assistant.

Ask Parrot picks its own brain

It answers with your reports AI by default. Pick Ollama for it instead, in Settings under Assistant, to keep it free and on your Mac.

Your language, too

Parrot hears the call in its own language and writes back in it.

Transcription
Auto-detects the language, or pin one in Settings, or pick the call's language under Start recording. For European languages, Parakeet v3 is a faster free model: 25 of them, no Turkish. Anything else goes to Whisper on its own. If a call turns out to be in another language, a banner says so and offers Switch or Keep.

Assistant and report
Written in the language of the call. Claude handles the most languages well.

Your documents
All of the languages above. Ask in English and it still finds the answer in a Turkish or Spanish document.

  • HelloEnglish
  • MerhabaTurkish
  • HolaSpanish
  • BonjourFrench
  • HalloGerman
  • CiaoItalian
  • OláPortuguese
  • HoiDutch
  • ПриветRussian
  • مرحباArabic
  • नमस्तेHindi
  • 你好Chinese
  • こんにちはJapanese
  • 안녕하세요Korean
  • and dozens more, auto-detected

Speaker names

Names, not Speaker 2.

Speaker detection that runs on your Mac. Parrot tells the voices on a call apart, asks you who they were, and knows them next time.

After the call, Parrot has told the voices apart. It asks who they were.

Told apart on your Mac

Speaker detection runs after the call with a 13 MB model. No audio goes anywhere to do it.

Name a voice once

Every line from that voice is renamed. One line in the wrong place? Move it from the line's right-click menu.

Sounds like Jeremy?

Turn on Remember voices and Parrot keeps a voiceprint on this Mac. Next call it suggests who's talking, and you confirm with one click. With your calendar connected, the people on the invite are one-click names too.

After the call

The report writes itself. Then it coaches you.

A meeting summary, action items and coaching, ready before you've hung up, with every point linked to the line it came from. Point at a section to see what it's for.

Northwind renewal

41 minSales discovery

How the call went

  2. 2Buying temp jumped after the SSO answer 12:20Play
  3. 3They asked about a pilot 38:10Play

Post-call report

Northwind is ready to move. Data residency and SSO are settled, and ten seats were quoted at $79 a seat on the annual plan.

Pain points

  • Legal won't sign until customer data is confirmed to stay in the EU.
  • Budget sign-off sits with someone who wasn't on the call.

Talk balance

You 48%Them 52%

Your speaking time against theirs. On a discovery call you want them doing most of the talking, and the coaching tells you when you didn't.

Objections & questions

  • Where is our customer data stored? 00:38Handled
  • What does the annual plan cost for ten seats? 01:10Handled
  • Can we start with one team as a pilot? 38:10Missed

What went well

  • Answered the data question in one breath, straight from the FAQ.

What to improve

  • Jeremy asked about a pilot at 38:10 and you moved on to pricing. Answer it in the follow-up.
  • Ask who signs off on budget before you wrap up.

Commitments & follow-ups

  • You: send the security summary and the DPA today.
  • Jeremy: confirm who signs off on budget.

Works with Claude

Your meetings, in Claude.

Ask the AI you already use about your calls. It's free, there's no meeting bot, and your own plan does the thinking.

Your AI app

What did I promise Northwind last week?

You made two promises to Northwind:

  • Send the security summary and the DPA. 12:34
  • Book the pilot kickoff with Jeremy. 41:07

Opens Parrot at that moment

Ask about your meetings

Connect in one click

Claude Desktop and Cursor connect with one click. Claude Code and Codex get a ready-made command. Find it under Claude & AI Apps in the sidebar.

Ask the AI you already use

"What did I promise last week?" "Brief me for my call with Acme." "Draft the follow-up." It gets real speaker names, promises with who owns them, and ready-made actions: weekly digest, follow-up email, prep for a call.

Off until you turn it on

It's read-only, and you choose what it sees. When you ask, the parts it reads go to that app's company under your account: Anthropic, OpenAI or Cursor's AI provider. That makes it a different mode from fully on your Mac. On-device-only meetings, audio and keys are never shown.

Privacy policyHow it works

Everything else

And the everyday stuff, done right.

The small things a call recorder should just do, so you never think about them.

Never loses a call

If Parrot crashes or gets force-quit mid-call, the recording comes back on next launch with its transcript and report.

Your mic, sorted

Echo cancellation keeps the call out of your mic on speakers. AirPods die mid-call? The mic reconnects by itself.

Names spelled right

Add your product, client and team names to a custom vocabulary and Whisper gets them right.

Notes on the side

Type notes during the call or after it. They're kept with the meeting and go out with the export.

Sends it where you work

Notes to your Obsidian vault, next steps to Reminders, a follow-up email draft, a webhook for Zapier or Make. All off until you switch them on.

One key away

⌘R to start, ⌘-period to stop, ⌘K to ask about past calls. ⌃⌥M marks a moment mid-call, even with Zoom in front.

Exact counts, no AI

"How many meetings last week?", "My 5 longest meetings", "Did I meet with Northwind?": Ask Parrot counts them on your Mac, exactly, with no AI.

Updates itself

Signed updates download in the background and install when you quit. Never during a call.

Bug reports in two clicks

The ladybug in the corner fills in your version and settings, then opens a GitHub issue for you to check.

Privacy

What leaves your Mac.

Two ways to run Parrot. You pick, you can mix them, and you can switch anytime.

Free · works offline

Fully on your Mac

Whisper transcribes, Ollama runs the Assistant and the reports. After a one-time model download, nothing leaves your Mac and the Wi-Fi can be off.

Sharper · a few cents an hour

With your own keys

Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Groq, Deepgram, TypeSafe. Requests go straight from your Mac to the provider you picked, on your own account. No Parrot server in between.

Most people mix: transcription on the Mac, live cards from Claude. Every setting says exactly what it sends.

Fully on your MacWith your own keys

Audio

Fully on your Mac

Never.

With your own keys

Only if you pick Groq or Deepgram for transcription. Otherwise it stays on your Mac.

Transcript text

Fully on your Mac

Never.

With your own keys

To the AI you picked, Claude or your own server, while the Assistant is on. With a TypeSafe key, the latest question and a few lines around it also go to TypeSafe. Pause stops it all.

Your documents

Fully on your Mac

Never. Indexed with Apple's own language framework.

With your own keys

Only the passages that match, sent with the question so the answer can quote them, and to TypeSafe if you added its key. The files themselves are never uploaded.

Past meetings

Fully on your Mac

Never. Ask Parrot searches them on this Mac.

With your own keys

A few matching excerpts, and this chat's recent messages, to write an Ask Parrot answer. On-device-only meetings stay out of both, even in earlier answers that used them. Never whole meetings, never audio.

Claude and other AI apps

Fully on your Mac

Never. Off until you turn it on.

With your own keys

Only if you turn it on: when you ask, the parts of your meetings the app reads, only what you share, go to that app's company. On-device-only meetings, audio and keys never do.

Your calendar

Fully on your Mac

Never. Read on this Mac, never changed.

With your own keys

Only if you let the Assistant read the invite: title, guests and notes. Off by default.

API keys

Fully on your Mac

None needed.

With your own keys

In your Mac's Keychain. Each key goes only to its own provider.

Parrot's servers

Fully on your Mac

There are none.

With your own keys

Still none. Nothing passes through us. There is no us.

Your controls

Every meeting says what left this Mac and where. Make one profile on-device only. Hide emails, phone and card numbers from cloud AI. Let old audio delete itself.

Connections

A notes folder, Reminders, a webhook, AI apps like Claude Desktop. All off until you turn them on, and on-device-only meetings are never sent.

Updates

One check a day to Parrot's update feed on GitHub, so you hear about fixes. It carries the app's version number and nothing about you.

Language models

For documents in Arabic, Indian scripts and sometimes Cyrillic, macOS downloads a language model from Apple once. It only downloads. Your documents are never uploaded.

Accounts, telemetry, analytics

None in the app, in either setup. There is nothing to phone home to.

The app never phones home. This website counts visits with Google Analytics, and only after you say yes.

There is nothing to certify because there is no server. The code is small enough to read in an afternoon, and the security policy asks you to try.

Read the security policy

  • About 24k lines of Swift
  • Three dependencies
  • Keys live in your Keychain
  • Releases signed and notarized

Open source

Read it. Fix it. Make it yours.

Native Swift, one repo, GPL-3.0. The whole app fits in an afternoon of reading, and FILEMAP.md tells you where everything is.

Where I could use a hand

  • Speaker detection with overlapping speech and similar voices
  • macOS permission edge cases around audio-capture taps
  • Bugs, ideas, and telling me I'm doing something wrong
git clone https://github.com/turantekin/Parrot.git
cd Parrot
make run

That compiles with swift build, assembles Parrot.app, signs it with whatever identity you have, and launches it.

FAQ

The questions people ask first.

Does a bot join my meeting?

No. Parrot records the sound your Mac already plays and hears, so nothing joins the call and nobody sees it in the participant list.

Is Parrot free?

Yes. Parrot is free and open source under GPL-3.0, with no account and no paid plan. If you add your own keys for cloud AI, you pay those providers directly, usually a few cents per hour of calls.

Does it work with Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams?

Yes, and with anything else your Mac can hear, like a phone on speaker. Parrot never connects to the meeting app itself.

Does Parrot start recording on its own?

Only if you ask it to. When Zoom, Meet, Teams or another call app starts using the mic, Parrot asks whether to record. You can switch that to record automatically, or off. It only sees that the mic is in use, never the other app's audio.

Can I search my past calls?

Yes. Press ⌘K and ask, like "What did I promise Acme?" The answer quotes the moment, and a click opens that call at the line. The search runs on your Mac. With a cloud AI, only a few matching excerpts go out to write the answer; with Ollama, nothing does.

Does it work with Claude or ChatGPT?

Yes. Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor and Codex (in the ChatGPT app) can read your meetings on your Mac, once you turn it on. Cloud-only agents can't reach it, because Parrot answers locally.

Use your meetings in Claude

Does my audio leave my Mac?

Not unless you choose it. Transcription, speaker detection and your documents run on your Mac. Audio is sent out only if you pick Groq or Deepgram for transcription. The live Assistant sends transcript text, never audio, to the AI you pick.

Does Parrot work offline?

Yes. With Whisper for transcription and Ollama for the Assistant, everything runs on your Mac and the Wi-Fi can be off. You need the internet once, to download the models.

Which Macs does it run on? Is there a Windows version?

The download needs macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon, so an M1 or newer. There is no Windows or Linux version.

Which AI models can I use?

For the live Assistant and reports: Claude, a local model through Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible server such as OpenAI, Gemini, Groq, OpenRouter or LM Studio. For transcription: Whisper on your Mac, Groq or Deepgram.

How is Parrot different from Granola, Otter and other AI note takers?

Most AI note takers send your call to their cloud and give you notes after it ends. Parrot keeps the audio on your Mac and helps while the call is still going, with answers from your own documents. It is also free and open source, so you can read exactly what it does.

Ready to try Parrot?

Your next call is the demo.

Free, no account, nothing to configure. Three steps and your next call has an assistant.

  • Open source, GPL-3.0
  • No account
  • No telemetry
  • Auto-detects your language
  • Signed and notarized
  • macOS 14+, Apple Silicon

  1. 1Download and choose how private

    One signed DMG. Pick Private, Balanced or Cloud on first launch, from fully on your Mac to Claude and Deepgram in the cloud.

  2. 2Allow two permissions

    System audio for the other side, microphone for yours. The welcome tour deep-links to the exact settings panes.

  3. 3Take your next call

    Start Google Meet, Zoom or Teams and Parrot asks to record. Or hit record yourself. The Assistant opens next to the live transcript.

From Uygar

Hi, I'm Uygar.

Parrot started as a tool for me and got a little out of hand, in the best way.

I run my businesses on calls: clients, partners, the odd supplier who swears the invoice is in the post. I tried the call recorders and meeting assistants. Each one was missing the feature I needed, hid it behind a plan I didn't want, or sent my client calls on a trip through someone else's cloud. So one evening I stopped waiting and started building.

It's been on every client call of mine since. It remembers what I promised, catches the questions I dodged, and keeps every word on my Mac. It felt too useful to keep to myself, so here it is, free and open source.

This is my first open source project, built with Claude as my coding buddy, mostly late at night. There will be rough edges. Tell me about them: open an issue, send a fix, or just tell me I'm doing it wrong. All three make Parrot better.

When I'm not on a call, I'm with family or shouting at a football match. Two teams, so double the heartbreak. Evidence on the left. Parrot doesn't record those, promise.

Uygar

It's free and stays free. If it saves your day once in a while, you can buy me a coffee. No pressure, the parrot eats seeds anyway.
